Subject: Proposal: Premium SLA addendum & dedicated capacity at renewal

Hi Sarah / Orion procurement team —

Thanks for the productive renewal check-in last week. Attached is a concise proposal for the renewal window (effective 2029-07-01) that bundles:

- Premium SLA addendum (99.95% availability, formalized incident response timelines, and p99 latency SLOs for production routes)
- Dedicated capacity uplift: +30% reserved GPU pool for steady-state throughput, burst credits for seasonal spikes
- Term adjustment: 12-month base with optional 12-month automatic renewal

Key asks for you: please confirm
1) target start date (we're proposing 1 Jul 2029)
2) whether procurement needs an updated quote line item (attached Quote_Orion_2029.xlsx)
3) if Ops needs a short technical review with our SEs before legal signs the addendum

I've attached the SLA_Addendum_v2.pdf with tracked changes for your legal and a short SLO matrix for ops reference. If you prefer, we can spin up a 30-minute technical call this week — Laura (cc'd) can walk through latency measurement, canaries, and fallback policies.

Next steps (proposal):
- Sarah: confirm procurement timeline and preferred PO date
- Orion Ops: request technical review if needed
- Redwood: prepare final addendum for signature and schedule onboarding for upgraded tier

Thanks,
Alex Martinez

1) Latency SLO definition: in SLA_Addendum_v2 the p99 is called out but not the measurement window (rolling 30d vs 7d). Can you confirm how you plan to measure and report?
2) Cost delta: procurement wants a simple line showing incremental annual cost for the premium SLA + reserved capacity. The attached quote looks detailed — could you add a one-line summary?

I copied Mike (Ops lead) — he'll want to run a short technical readout with your SEs. Mike, can you do 30 minutes Thursday?

Alex / team / Orion —

Quick technical clarifications to address Sarah's questions and to prepare for the ops call:

- Measurement window: Redwood reports SLOs on a rolling 30-day window by default and publishes daily SLO health. For contract language we can add both a 7-day operational alert threshold (for faster on-call triggers) and a 30-day contractual measurement for compliance.

- Latency spec: for the premium tier we propose p95 < 120ms and p99 < 320ms for 1k-token requests on our recommended model family (we've tuned the kernel selection and batching to optimize tail latency). For short-generation routes (<128 tokens) we can guarantee p99 < 250ms. We'll include fallback to a slightly lower-cost model variant (with automatic regional routing) if burst capacity is exhausted to preserve availability.

- Validation & canary: recommend a 48-hour canary with synthetic traffic and a production prompt-set that Orion provides. We'll export KV cache hit rates & per-route latency histograms to a shared dashboard during the canary.

- Billing visibility: Marissa (cc'd) can set up a token-level cost export and a monthly committed-usage reconciliation to verify the reserved capacity billing.

I attached a compact SLO matrix (redwood-slo-matrix.png) to illustrate the measurement windows and alert thresholds we typically include in addenda.

I'll be available for a 30-minute call Thu 16:00-17:30 UTC — Alex, can you confirm?

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Sarah / Mike / Procurement —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Short summary and agreed next steps:

- Measurement: contractual p99 will be measured on a rolling 30-day window; we will add an operational 7-day alert threshold as Laura suggested.
- Latency guarantees: premium tier = p95 < 120ms, p99 < 320ms for 1k-token routes; short routes (<128 tokens) p99 < 250ms.
- Validation: 48-hour canary with synthetic traffic + shared dashboard for KV cache hit rates and histograms.
- Pricing: attached Quote_Orion_2029.xlsx — procurement, the one-line incremental annual cost is in cell A6 ("Premium SLA + reserved capacity: $162,000/yr"). I'll follow up with a clean PDF quote if you need it.

Action items:
- Sarah/procurement: confirm PO target week (you mentioned week of 20 May)
- Orion Ops (Mike): accept or propose an alternative time for the 30-minute technical review (Laura available Thu 16:00-17:30 UTC)
- Redwood legal: prepare final SLA addendum for signature once procurement confirms PO date (Marissa, can you please coordinate legal & billing?)

If procurement wants, I can also prepare a short amendment that toggles the canary requirement off for customers who have a dedicated private deployment — just say the word.

Thanks all — looking forward to closing RDW-3349.
